final.executive_summary: Trim AAPL to a 0.12 weight of total account equity at the next session open, selling roughly 25 shares (~$7,900 notional, ~$8 in fees) while retaining a core position. Do not exit and do not add at 312.41: the tape is below the 10-EMA (317.58), VWMA (320.95), and Bollinger mid (323.53), with an unfilled 310.69–333.43 gap overhead and only ~1.7:1 reward/risk to gap fill versus the 300 floor. Rebuild only on a close above 317.58 on >65M shares and subsequent VWMA/Bollinger confirmation; cut further if 300 breaks on >60M shares, and reassess the full weight at the late-October FY26 10-K.
final.investment_thesis: The debate supports reducing AAPL, not liquidating it. The Research Manager and Trader are right that the franchise print is strong — Q3 FY26 revenue +16.4%, gross margin 50.06%, operating income +26.6%, nine-month FCF $110.2B, net cash up ~$28.5B — which rules out Sell. But the bear case wins the trade at today's price on three points. First, the aggressive analyst is correct that the margin-reversion arithmetic was materially mis-sized: ~$2.2B is roughly one quarter of gross profit, not annualized, so a two-point gross-margin reversion is closer to ~$8.8–9B annualized, or ~5–6% of pre-tax income, not the ~3% used to dismiss it. Second, the +8.6% COGS line is locked for a quarter ended 27 June, while management's own commentary on rising memory prices and the blocked CXMT sourcing route is a forward cost headwind not yet in the P&L; 50.06% is at least as plausibly a mix/timing peak as a new plateau. Third, the tape is unambiguous: spot 312.41 is below the 10-EMA 317.58, below VWMA 320.95, below the Bollinger mid 323.53, with an entirely unfilled 310.69–333.43 gap overhead; the bounce from 302.56 came on decaying volume 75.1M → 68.0M → 49.4M → 46.1M versus 107.0M/261.8M at the June lows the bull cites; and MACD has decayed from 9.61 to 1.38 in six sessions. The neutral analyst correctly rejects the aggressive reload plan, because a first close above 317.58 would still be below VWMA and the Bollinger mid and would be a test of overhead supply, not proof the gap is repaired. But the conservative analyst over-insures by cutting to 0.08: the account is already ~80% cash, AAPL is a high-quality franchise with a rising 200-SMA, and prior lessons — especially the 2026-07-30 Underweight that worked (-6.3% raw, -9.9% alpha) but also the repeated 2026-07 Underweights and AMZN/GOOGL cases that were hurt by excessive pre-catalyst trimming — argue for a moderate trim, not a near-exit. I therefore adopt the neutral analyst's 0.12 target rather than the trader's 0.13 or the conservative's 0.08: it is modestly more gap-aware than 0.13 without treating a 35% bear tail as the base case. The unverified 31 July gap cause, the $13.3B net intangibles increase, the ~$15–23B unexplained equity jump, the unverified departing-CEO descriptor, the OpenAI injunction, deferred revenue growth lagging revenue, and the tax-rate step-up all argue for carrying a smaller core into the late-October 10-K, but they do not prove the bear's ~20% downside scenario. What would change the call: a daily close above 317.58 on >65M shares followed by a hold above VWMA 320.95 and Bollinger mid 323.53 would justify rebuilding toward 0.16–0.18; a reclaim and successful retest of 333.43 would support 0.18–0.20; a daily close below 300 on >60M shares would justify cutting toward 0.06–0.08 or flat depending on the next open; and Q4 FY26 gross margin below 48% would break the margin-holds premise. The conditions are narrative only, not implemented orders.
